rows.name: TRACED_NOTIFY_FD
rows.read_by: `perfetto/launcher-common` sets it for `traced` (the Perfetto tracing service). The only reader in TRON is a fake `traced` that `perfetto/test_perfetto.py` writes.
rows.values: A file descriptor number. `perfetto/launcher-common` sets `3`.

rows.name: TRACED_PROBES_NOTIFY_FD

new_terms.definition: The script that LSF starts on the worker server for one job of Distributed Dice. It starts the command of the job there.
The host mode in which one Dice daemon serves all users of the server. The file `/etc/positron/dice.yaml` selects it with `mode: shared`.
The script that submits a build command to an LSF worker. The remote job starts with an empty environment. The script passes on a fixed list of variables.
The installer of Rust toolchains. `rust/rust-toolchain.sh` runs it outside the Nix dev shell.
A third-party I/O tool. A copy is in `bin/iotools-1.5`. No TRON build file builds it.
The Linux driver that gives a user program direct access to a PCI device, such as an FPGA card.
The two Perfetto daemons. `traced` is the tracing service. `traced_probes` collects kernel events.
The two launcher scripts for Perfetto traces. They start the Perfetto programs. Both load `perfetto/launcher-common`.
The compiler tool that reports data races at run time. `make test-tsan` runs the test programs in `gen-tsan` that are built with it.
The file that `rust/rust-toolchain.sh` writes. `rust/run-cargo` reads it outside Nix to find the Rust installation.
The Python package tool. `bin/ci/check-lock-freshness.sh` runs `uv lock --check` on the `uv.lock` files of the repository.
The development environment that `nix develop .#lint` starts. It holds the pinned lint tools.
The pytest suites under `t/proxy`. They send recorded conversations to a `rinzler_proxy` process on `127.0.0.1`.

notes: No row is dropped. The proxy rows (`all_proxy`, `http_proxy`, `https_proxy`, `no_proxy`), `USERNAME`, `TEMP` and `TMP` depend on rules of the Python standard library. Those rules are not in the checkout. They were read and tested in Python 3.10.12 outside the checkout: `urllib.request.getproxies_environment`, `getpass.getuser` and `tempfile`. The httpx library was not available to read. The statements on httpx rest on `t/proxy/README.md` and on a comment in `t/proxy/test_rzproxy.py`. The input did not list `bin/ci/hf_cache.py` as a `urllib` user. The rows `https_proxy` and `no_proxy` add it. `tron_use` counts test code as TRON code. So `TRACED_NOTIFY_FD` and `TRACED_PROBES_NOTIFY_FD` are `reads and sets`: the launcher sets them, and the only reader is a fake daemon in `perfetto/test_perfetto.py`. `shellHook` stays as a row: a test reads it from the process environment. The `TMPDIR` row names the files that use the name. It does not list every `mktemp`, `tempfile` or `temp_directory_path` call. Evidence quotes avoid source lines that hold a pipe character.
